plate_findings.evidence: Caption: "macroglossia"; the photograph visibly shows a prominently enlarged protruding tongue.
Caption: "ear lobe creases"; linear indentation is visible in the earlobe.
Caption: "pit on posterior helix"; a small posterior helical pit is visible.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of a patient with characteristic Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome macroglossia and captioned facial/tongue hemihyperplasia. B: Clinical close-up showing the captioned earlobe crease characteristic of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. C: Clinical close-up showing the captioned posterior helix pit characteristic of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome.

panels.figure_caption: Common phenotypes associated with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome: A) macroglossia and facial/tongue hemihyperplasia, B) ear lobe creases, C) pit on posterior helix.
in_text_mentions: Macroglossia, together with omphalocele or other umbilical abnormalities, allows recognition of the disorder at birth. Sometimes hemihyperplasia is not present at birth but becomes apparent later in childhood. It can be noted in approximately 12.5% of the cases and is present in 40% of the children who develop tumors (Figure 1).9
